newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAKS PASS CONTROVERSIAL EDUCATION LAW AMENDMENT.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAKS PASS CONTROVERSIAL EDUCATION LAW AMENDMENT.

text.p: The Slovak parliament on Thursday approved a controversial amendment to the law on higher education, giving the Education Ministry broader powers to act in the affairs of universities.
The law, approved by 75 of the 130 deputies present, gives the ministry the right to cancel decisions of university scientific councils, including the granting academic titles.
It also gives the ministry a say in the process of creating or closing existing university faculties.

The law has come under fierce criticism by oposition deputies, as well as the country's academic representatives, who say it violates the principle of academic freedom and has an anti-democratic spirit.

"The proposed paragraph (on the ministry's decisive powers)... is a ruthless interference into the autonomy of universities and academic rights and freedoms of their authorities and individuals," Slovak university chiefs said in an open letter addressed to the government and parliament.
Minister of Education, Eva Slavkovska, rejected the criticism, however, saying the ministry had no intention to cast doubts on professional decisions of the academic bodies.
"However, the ministry must have an opportunity to decide in a case if the university breaches the law or general regulations," she told parliament prior to the vote.
In July, Madelaine Albright, U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations, conveyed U.S.concerns of some legislative moves by the Slovak government, including the education law amendment.

Immediately after the vote, opposition deputies said they had collected the neccesary minimum of 30 signatures, to demand an extra-ordinary session of parliament, with the only item on the agenda to be a non-confidence vote on Slavkovska.

But Slavkovska, a member of the junior governing coalition partner, the ultra-right Slovak National Party, has the support of Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar's Movement for a Democractic Slovakia (HZDS) and is expected to survive any non-confidence vote.
